one_month_reasoning: No full earnings in the window: Q3 2026 results are expected ~Nov 9-10, after Oct 31. In-window possibilities: (1) a company release confirming CB-4 first-hall rent commencement (targeted late Sept; no release through Oct 1, src 25) - expected and mostly priced; (2) launch of the ~$3.5B Morgan Stanley-led Justified debt (expected 'before year-end', src 27) - pricing terms could move the stock either way; (3) a preliminary Q3 print or deal release, as TeraWulf did on Oct 28 2025 (src 26) - a two-sided tail; (4) Oct 28 FOMC and AI-infrastructure sector beta, which has been negative (below 50d/200d MAs, insiders net sellers). Anthropic IPO marketing likely starts after the window. With no scheduled earnings I stay near symmetric around spot: lognormal median ~$14.70 (slight downward tilt for negative momentum) and monthly sigma ~27% (91%/3.5 plus a little for the possible financing/preliminary-results release). Round 3: the GPU-life rebuild changes only long-dated (2032+) cash flows and moves fair value by ~$0.3, which does not move a one-month distribution, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged. Round 4: the site and discount-rate rebuild moves long-dated value and the pipeline, not anything scheduled before Oct 31, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend at 2027-10-01: site-by-site split-rate DCF $8.84 (50%; contracted in-term flows at 8.5% Fluidstack / 9.25% Core42 and Anthropic, everything else at 10% WACC; single-rate $8.18), cap-rate SOTP $11.0 (30%) and 12x 2028E EBITDA $9.4 (20%), all now including the same per-site pipeline values ($1.35B at 6/30/26, net of Muskie liabilities). Blend $9.6 (round 3 $7.7).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site DCF with split discounting, valued at 6/30/26 and rolled at Ke 13.3% to 10/1/27. Contracted in-term cash flows: Fluidstack CB-3/4/5 (378 MW, $7.2B over 10-yr terms incl. July 2026 amendments; yr-1 $1.70M/MW +2.5%/yr; starts Jul-26/Dec-26/May-27) at 8.5%; Core42 (60 MW, $1.1B/10 yrs, $110M/yr less $50.6M prepaid offset) and Anthropic/Justified (401 MW, $707M yr-1 +3%, 20 yrs) at 9.25%; their build capex and corporate G&A at the same contracted rates. Post-term (extension options exercised 78% at the escalated schedule, else 1 yr dark and re-let at 85%: factor 0.967), $0.75M/MW retrofit at LM renewal, terminal (2% g, retrofit reserve) and the probability-weighted pipeline (LM expansion, Lake Hawkeye, Muskie, Chesapeake, net of $11M/MW capex, Muskie liabilities/collateral and the Chesapeake price) at 10.0% WACC. 83% NOI, 3% maintenance capex, 21% tax from 2030. Bridge: $5.725B debt - $3.0B cash - $0.5B Abernathy proceeds; Justified NCI = max(6.8% of Justified NPV, ~$102M fixed put) = $0.15B; 612.9M shares. Result $8.84 (single 10% rate $8.18); contracted-only $6.26 (single $5.61). GPU life 4/5/6/7 yrs: $8.26/8.84/9.15/9.44. WACC 9.5/10.5%: $10.7/$7.23. Fluidstack rate 8.0/9.0%: $8.88/$8.79.

inputs_detail.input: Contracted discount rate: Fluidstack in-term cash flows
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: the $3.2B WULF Compute notes secured on these leases cost 7.75% coupon / 8.7% effective (10-Q), BB at issue in Oct 2025 when the 10Y was ~4.1%. Treasuries are ~110bp higher (10Y 5.24%), but Google (Aa2/AA+) backstops ~$3.2B of $7.2B effective lease by lease at commencement ($600M live after CB-3), completion risk falls away as halls commence, and an unverified quote page shows the notes yielding ~6.4-6.6%. The rate must also carry the equity slice under 68% debt, operating risk and the ~56% unbacked share, so I use 8.5%, just under the effective note cost. 8.0%/9.0% give ${N['fs80']}/${N['fs90']}: the in-term rent is largely offset by its own build capex and G&A discounted at the same rate.

inputs_detail.input: Contracted discount rate: Core42 and Anthropic in-term cash flows
inputs_detail.derivation: Both counterparties are unrated with no IG support in force: Core42 has no backstop (energized, so no completion risk); Anthropic's support is only 'expected to be' IG, construction has not started and the planned $3.5B package is leveraged loans plus high yield, i.e. sub-IG cost (the terminated bridge was SOFR+275bp). Set between the Fluidstack rate (8.5%) and WACC (10%).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Stabilized NOI $1.131B / 7.5% cap = $15.09B, discounted to $13.39B at 10/1/27, less $1.86B remaining Justified capex, $6.15B net debt (adds the $150M fit-out), $0.15B Justified NCI, plus $1.52B site-by-site pipeline (the DCF's per-site values for LM expansion, Lake Hawkeye, Muskie net of its liabilities, Chesapeake net of price, rolled to 10/1/27) = $6.75B / 612.9M = $11.0.

inputs_detail.derivation: LM 2028 rent from the site build.
Unchanged.

bear.story: The market prices WULF at or below contracted-only value (~$5.61-6.26 single vs split rate, before pipeline): the Justified $3.5B debt prices expensively or needs equity, Anthropic IG support is not finalized, CB-5/Justified slip, a GPU-supply glut (Rubin volume, cheaper power) revives worries about re-leasing rents after the 10-yr Fluidstack terms, and AI-capex digestion with a >5% 10Y keeps landlords derated. Muskie stays untenanted into the ESA in-service date, putting ~$0.6B of collateral at risk.

base.story: CB-4/CB-5 deliver (Lake Mariner run-rate ~$0.8B by mid-2027), the Justified debt prices on acceptable terms, first Anthropic capacity arrives H2'27, and perhaps one modest new lease is signed. The stock keeps a pipeline premium over the ~$9.6 fundamental value but drifts slightly below spot as dilution and leverage build. GPU-life debate stays a neocloud issue; for a landlord it trims long-dated value only modestly. Muskie or Lake Mariner expansion is the likeliest first new lease; NY sites stay stuck on EO 62 and local opposition.

bull.story: A new 250-500 MW hyperscaler/AI-lab lease (Muskie or Lake Mariner expansion), an Anthropic IPO halo on tenant credit, and a sector re-rate toward consensus targets (~$33) at ~15x+ steady-state NOI. Persistent compute scarcity (A100s re-contracted into 2029) supports renewal at or above escalated rents.

thesis_break_reason: $5.5 is below the contracted-only DCF on both bases (single 10% $5.61, split $6.26) and gives zero credit for the pipeline (~$2.6/sh at the horizon, net of Muskie liabilities) or the lower contracted discount rate. A sustained trade there would most likely mean a fundamental problem: a failed or punitive Justified financing or dilutive rescue raise, failure of Anthropic's IG support, a Fluidstack payment event beyond the Google backstop, or CB-4/CB-5 commencement failing so the backstop never becomes effective. It is ~63% below spot, beyond what 91%-vol noise usually explains.

key_uncertainties: Justified financing and Anthropic's credit support: the ~$3.5B debt is unpriced and IG support is 'expected', not final; this sets both the 9.25% contracted rate and dilution.
Discount rates: WACC 9.5/10.5% gives $10.7/$7.23 on the DCF; the contracted-rate split adds ~$0.65 (Fluidstack rate 8.0-9.0% moves it < $0.1 because build capex is discounted at the same rate).
Pipeline conversion: Muskie (55%/35% tranches) carries ~$0.6B of utility collateral at risk; NY sites face EO 62 and the Lansing draft ban; Chesapeake price is undisclosed.
Commencement timing: CB-4 first hall unconfirmed as of Oct 2; the Google backstop only becomes effective at commencement.
Margin: 85% NOI is a target; Q2 adjusted ~80%.
Post-contract value: extension exercise odds and retrofit costs after 2036-37; 4-7 yr GPU-life cases span $8.26-9.44.
Escalators (Fluidstack, Anthropic) and the Justified put amount are undisclosed.
91% realized vol and AI-infra sector beta dominate the 12-month distribution.
reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the checked inventory (src 40) so every site appears once: Core42 60 MW and Fluidstack CB-3/4/5 378 MW (not 440/380) with each building's commencement, the $7.2B Fluidstack total including the July 2026 amendments (+$0.7/sh), the $150M parent-funded fit-out (-$0.28), Core42's prepaid-rent offset, the Fluidstack extension options at the escalated schedule (verified on the company release; renewal factor 0.91 -> 0.967, +$0.4), the unbacked share fixed to 56%, mining as a wind-down with no double-counted MW, Abernathy as proceeds only, and the Justified NCI as max(6.8% of project NPV, ~$102M fixed put) instead of 6.8% of firm EV. Pipeline sites are now in the DCF, probability-weighted at WACC net of $11M/MW capex: LM expansion 35%, Lake Hawkeye 15% (Lansing draft ban, EO 62), Muskie 55%/35% net of $288M of acquisition liabilities and expected collateral forfeiture (the ESA's 20-yr minimum charges make the collateral a real exit cost), Chesapeake ~21% net of an assumed price and generation capex. Together they add $2.58/sh. Split discounting: Fluidstack in-term flows at 8.5% (anchored on the 8.7% effective WULF Compute secured notes), Core42 and Anthropic at 9.25%, everything else at 10%. Contracted-only DCF $5.61 single -> $6.26 split; with the pipeline $8.18 -> $8.84. The split is worth only ~$0.65 because build capex and G&A are discounted at the same lower rate and ~45% of value is post-term. Round-3 DCF $5.8 -> $8.84: most of the rise is the pipeline moving into the DCF (+$2.6) and the split (+$0.65). SOTP $11.2 -> $11.0 and EV/EBITDA $7.3 -> $9.4 (pipeline now added there too, fit-out and NCI fixed). Blend $7.7 -> $9.6. Because most of the fair-value change comes from moving the pipeline between methods rather than from new information, I raised only the base scenario ($12.8 -> $13.3, weights 30/45/25 unchanged) and moved the mid-ladder up ~1.5pp (P >= spot 0.386 -> 0.401). The thesis break stays at $5.5, below contracted-only value on both bases. 1-month ladder unchanged. Research: 2 searches and 4 fetches (10-Q, Q2 deck, Q2 call, Fluidstack release); the secondary-market quote on the WULF Compute notes is single-source and only nudged the rate.

discounting.basis: Contracted in-term cash flows from the Google-backstopped Fluidstack leases at 8.5%, anchored on the 8.7% effective cost of the $3.2B WULF Compute notes secured on them (7.75% coupon, BB at issue), adjusted for higher Treasuries (+~110bp since Oct 2025) against a backstop that becomes effective lease by lease, falling completion risk and an unverified secondary quote near 6.5%. Unrated counterparties at 9.25%: Core42 (no backstop) and Anthropic (IG support only 'expected', unfinanced construction; planned debt is leveraged loan + HY). Each project's build capex and corporate G&A are discounted at the contracted rates (conservative). Post-term, pipeline, mining and terminal at the 10.0% WACC. Contracted-only: split $6.26 vs single $5.61. The split adds only ~$0.65/sh because the in-term rent is largely offset by build capex and G&A discounted at the same lower rate, and because ~45% of value sits post-term or in the terminal.
